answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, weighting identities by independently supported paths rather than raw count. A sybil cluster can form a violet-marked island connected to honest nodes by a narrow inlet: its sparse external cut yields low conductance, trapping walk mass. Given a defined degree and restart model, this bottleneck mathematically bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; the bound depends on cut size and volume, not its members’ labels.
